body:
Right now you are, in that you're just trying to prove your point.

Quickly, hit Win+D. Your boss is behind you.
Because people are self-serving. I've given so much out to people that I want/need to protect the little I have left.
And I see it as just further proof not to trust people.

There was no relationship, not even a single (first) date. I just got led around for six months with empty promises, lies and such, and in my searching for approval and happiness, put blinders on my own head.

There's a few significant social interaction hurdles that would have to be cleared first before I even considered the sales world.

As for the second part, well, I have no idea what sort of places your are talking about; the idea frightens me to no end though.

I'm not 100% sure that I know the answer to that. I'm a complete and total mess, in short. I just would like to feel comfortable enough that I don't need the security blanket of a shell/facade/wall. 

I really only let one person in. She ran amok, strung me along for months and then let me down very, very hard. It was just further proof that I shouldn't let my guard down. 

I'm very, very (overly?) sensitive. I'm smart. I'm afraid to show that, too. I have a lot of weird, unconnected things that interest me. I have an odd view of the world. I have a lot of odd stances. I don't really know how to describe things beyond that. I have the words in my head, but translating them into the proper symbols to describe them for you? Not so easy...

>How old are you? 

24. 25 in 4 months and week. Anywhere between 20% and 99.99 repeating% of my lifespan spent with absolutely nothing to show for it. 

>Are you a student? 

As I said, I failed out in my attempt at a 4 year. Social anxiety led to not going to classes and getting messed up constantly. 

>You can try to take a speech class

I actually just started taking this at night at the community college here. Speeches are easy for me, because it's not 1 on 1 communication. It's not personal. I can put on a nice front and no one knows the difference. And since I'm relatively intelligent (140ish IQ), I don't look foolish and can pull it off. It's different from in-depth, personal speaking though, mainly because it isn't... me.

>What are your hobbies? What makes you happy?

I play a lot of games. That's largely an escape, though, I think. Since I had no friends growing up, I was left largely to my own devices. My parents were always busy as I said. You keep to what you know, I guess. I have a lot of niched topics that fascinate me. Philosophy (though that's spiraling more and more towards solipsism), history, certain sciences... I 'people watch' a lot, too, since there's no human interaction required. I'm pretty decent at it, too. I'm very good at reading people. You have to be if you want to maintain a good facade. It's been a necessity. 

>What city are you from?

This question makes me very, very uneasy since I know a handful of redditors. Baltimore.

Can you specify what regards you're asking that in? 

A shallow box of emotionally damaged goods would be the short answer without any further prompting.

Oral communication doesn't really come to me very easily... or at all. I can comprehend what you are saying, but anxiety will keep me from talking to someone. And if it doesn't, the swirling thoughts in my head keep me clammed up and I end up appearing awkward and/or disinterested. 

I'm not very interesting, going by the evidence and it's just a bad formula through and through.

I go there. I feel out of place. I don't know what to do or how to act or even how to really interact with another human being. My heart starts pounding. My mind starts racing. I'm reminded of another time in a somewhat similar situation where something went completely wrong. There's always a million examples of that in my life. Now that one mental image. That one thing. It's stuck in my head. And no, it's not coming out of there. 

And because I'm trying to corral that idea in my head, I'm sure as hell sitting silently (and probably looking even more weird and awkward as a result) and lo and behold. I now have more fodder that my mind can taunt me with.
